name: Chora
tagline: The port town under the Venetian castle, with the Portara offshore
description: Naxos town, climbing from the harbour through whitewashed lanes to the Venetian kastro, with the enormous marble Portara standing on the islet at the harbour mouth. It has the shops, the banks, the ferries and the widest choice of housing, and it works year-round.
bestFor: Anyone staying past the season who needs a town that keeps functioning
pros: Everything open year-round, including services and supermarkets
The Portara, the kastro and the harbour all on foot
All ferries and bus routes leave from here
cons: The highest rents on the island
Ferry arrivals at all hours in summer

name: Agios Prokopios and Agia Anna
tagline: The main beach strip, five minutes south of town
description: The sand beaches immediately south of Chora, backed by low-rise studios, tavernas and beach bars, with a bus every twenty minutes into town. It is the most convenient beach base on the island: swimming from the doorstep with the town's services still close.
bestFor: Summer stays that want the beach and the town both within reach
pros: Frequent buses to Chora in ten minutes
Tavernas and beach bars along the strip
cons: Very busy in July and August

name: Halki and the Tragea Valley
tagline: The old inland capital among the olive groves
description: The village at the centre of the Tragea, a broad valley of olive groves and Byzantine churches in the island's interior, with a distillery producing the local citron liqueur and a handful of tavernas. It is the greenest part of Naxos and the most agricultural, twenty minutes from town.
bestFor: Long stays wanting village life, olive groves and a proper local price
pros: Genuinely rural and green, unlike most Cyclades
Long-term rents well below the coast
Byzantine churches and walking routes throughout the valley
cons: A car or scooter is essential
Twenty minutes to the nearest beach

name: Apeiranthos and the Mountain Villages
tagline: Marble-paved lanes high on Mount Zas
description: A stone village built on the slopes of Mount Zas with marble-paved lanes, Venetian towers and its own dialect, one of the most distinctive settlements in the Cyclades. It is cool in summer, remote in winter, and the trail to the island's highest point starts nearby.
bestFor: Stays that want the mountain, cool air and a genuinely traditional village
pros: Cool in summer and genuinely atmospheric
Mount Zas trails and the Zeus cave nearby
The lowest long-term rents on the island
cons: Half an hour of mountain road to Chora
Very limited services and slow internet

name: Plaka and the Southwest Coast
tagline: The long empty beaches down the western shore
description: The four-kilometre run of sand south of Agia Anna, backed by dunes and cedar rather than development, with scattered studios and a few tavernas. It is the emptiest accessible beach on Naxos and the most exposed, which means space in August and wind whenever the meltemi blows.
bestFor: Stays that want an empty beach and are content to drive for everything else
pros: Four kilometres of largely empty sand
Dunes and cedar rather than hotel blocks
Quiet even at the height of summer
cons: Very exposed when the meltemi blows
Almost everything closes out of season
